title: How much ribbon does each of two friends get?
description: Twenty nine metres of ribbon is shared equally between two friends. The leftover metre is shared too, and one half is changed into the decimal zero point five. Keeko's doubt is that the sharing stops at fourteen metres.
teaching_notes: One idea: a leftover can be shared again by writing it as a fraction and changing the bottom to ten. Watch for students who stop at the remainder and forget the part metre.

source: Ziva shares 29 m of ribbon equally with Jia. How much does
video_script.why: The child can divide counting numbers with a remainder but has not shared the remainder as a decimal.
video_script.substitution: Half a metre is five tenths, which is zero point five metres.
video_script.anchor: Ziva shares twenty nine metres of red ribbon equally with Jia
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko stops at fourteen metres each and treats the one metre left over as lost, though it can be cut in half.
video_script.payoff_line: Each of them gets fourteen point five metres of ribbon.
video_script.fraction_reading: A fraction such as 1/2 is read one half, and 5/10 is read five over ten.

names.Ziva: shares twenty nine metres of red ribbon

maths_rules: the remaining 1 m shared by two gives 1/2 m each

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a red ribbon is twenty nine metres long. It is shared equally between two friends.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find how much ribbon each friend gets.

beats.on_screen: 29 ÷ 2: each gets 14 m, 1 m remains; the 1 m shared by two gives 1/2 m each

marks.s1a: 29 ÷ 2 is written and fourteen metres goes to each friend
marks.s1b: the last metre is cut in the middle, one half for each

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>Step one, share the whole metres. Each friend gets fourteen metres, and one metre remains.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Share that last metre between the two. Each friend gets one half of a metre more.

marks.s2b: the top and bottom are multiplied by 5 to give 5/10

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Step two, change one half into a decimal. The bottom must be ten, a hundred or a thousand.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Two times five is ten, so multiply the top and the bottom by five. One half becomes five over ten.
<bookmark mark='s2c'/>Five over ten is zero point five.

marks.s3a: 14 and 0.5 are written with a plus sign and the sum left blank

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Step three, add the whole metres and the part metre. We add fourteen and zero point five.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>Each of them gets fourteen point five metres of ribbon.

narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's bubble shows 14 m each with 1 m left over; the leftover metre glows and is cut in the middle; the bubble is crossed out

marks.doubt: the bubble with 14 m and 1 m left over appears
marks.fix: the leftover metre glows and is cut in the middle
marks.right: each half metre is added to the share of fourteen metres

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each of them gets fourteen metres, and one metre is lost.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a metre of ribbon can still be cut. Cut it in the middle, and each of them gets half a metre.
<bookmark mark='right'/>A leftover can always be shared as a part, so the share is more than fourteen metres.
